# Pragmatism Is the Empiricist Attitude in a More Radical Form

Pragmatism represents a perfectly familiar attitude in philosophy, the empiricist attitude, but it represents it,[^1] both in a more radical and in a less objectionable form than it has ever yet assumed.[^2] A pragmatist turns his back resolutely and once for all upon a lot of inveterate habits dear to professional philosophers.[^3] He turns away from abstraction and insufficiency, from verbal solutions, from bad a priori reasons, from fixed principles, closed systems, and pretended absolutes and origins.[^4] He turns towards concreteness and adequacy, towards facts, towards action, and towards power.[^5] That means the empiricist temper regnant, and the rationalist temper sincerely given up.[^6] It means the open air and possibilities of nature, as against dogma, artificiality and the pretence of finality in truth.[^7]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Pragmatism represents a perfectly familiar attitude in philosophy, the empiricist attitude, but it represents it,"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "both in a more radical and in a less objectionable form than it has ever yet assumed."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "A pragmatist turns his back resolutely and once for all upon a lot of inveterate habits dear to professional philosophers."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "He turns away from abstraction and insufficiency, from verbal solutions, from bad a priori reasons, from fixed principles, closed systems, and pretended absolutes and origins."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "He turns towards concreteness and adequacy, towards facts, towards action, and towards power."
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "That means the empiricist temper regnant, and the rationalist temper sincerely given up."
[^7]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "It means the open air and possibilities of nature, as against dogma, artificiality and the pretence of finality in truth."

# Pragmatism Is a Method Only

At the same time[^1] pragmatism[^2] does not stand for any special results.[^3] It is a method only.[^4] But the general triumph of that method would mean an enormous change in[^5] the 'temperament' of philosophy.[^6] Teachers of the ultra-rationalistic type would be frozen out.[^7] Science and metaphysics would come much nearer together, would in fact work absolutely hand in hand.[^8]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "At the same time"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "pragmatism"
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "does not stand for any special results."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "It is a method only."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "But the general triumph of that method would mean an enormous change in"
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "the 'temperament' of philosophy."
[^7]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Teachers of the ultra-rationalistic type would be frozen out"
[^8]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Science and metaphysics would come much nearer together, would in fact work absolutely hand in hand."

# Solving Names Do Not End the Quest

Metaphysics has usually followed a very primitive kind of quest.[^1] The universe has always appeared to the natural mind as a kind of enigma, of which the key must be sought in the shape of some illuminating or power-bringing word or name.[^2] That word names the universe's PRINCIPLE, and to possess it is, after a fashion, to possess the universe itself.[^3] 'God,' 'Matter,' 'Reason,' 'the Absolute,' 'Energy,' are so many solving names.[^4] You can rest when you have them.[^5] You are at the end of your metaphysical quest.[^6]

But if you follow the pragmatic method, you cannot look on any such word as closing your quest.[^7] You must bring out of each word its practical cash-value, set it at work within the stream of your experience.[^8] It appears less as a solution, then, than as a program for more work, and more particularly as an indication of the ways in which existing realities may be CHANGED.[^9]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Metaphysics has usually followed a very primitive kind of quest."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "the universe has always appeared to the natural mind as a kind of enigma, of which the key must be sought in the shape of some illuminating or power-bringing word or name."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "That word names the universe's PRINCIPLE, and to possess it is, after a fashion, to possess the universe itself."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "'God,' 'Matter,' 'Reason,' 'the Absolute,' 'Energy,' are so many solving names."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "You can rest when you have them."
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "You are at the end of your metaphysical quest."
[^7]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "But if you follow the pragmatic method, you cannot look on any such word as closing your quest."
[^8]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "You must bring out of each word its practical cash-value, set it at work within the stream of your experience."
[^9]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "It appears less as a solution, then, than as a program for more work, and more particularly as an indication of the ways in which existing realities may be CHANGED."

# Theories Become Instruments, Not Answers to Enigmas

THEORIES THUS BECOME INSTRUMENTS, NOT ANSWERS TO ENIGMAS, IN WHICH WE CAN REST.[^1] We don't lie back upon them, we move forward, and, on occasion, make nature over again by their aid.[^2] Pragmatism unstiffens all our theories, limbers them up and sets each one at work.[^3] Being nothing essentially new, it harmonizes with many ancient philosophic tendencies.[^4] It agrees with nominalism for instance, in always appealing to particulars; with utilitarianism in emphasizing practical aspects; with positivism in its disdain for verbal solutions, useless questions, and metaphysical abstractions.[^5]

All these, you see, are ANTI-INTELLECTUALIST tendencies.[^6] Against rationalism as a pretension and a method, pragmatism is fully armed and militant.[^7] But, at the outset, at least, it stands for no particular results.[^8] It has no dogmas, and no doctrines save its method.[^9]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "THEORIES THUS BECOME INSTRUMENTS, NOT ANSWERS TO ENIGMAS, IN WHICH WE CAN REST."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "We don't lie back upon them, we move forward, and, on occasion, make nature over again by their aid."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Pragmatism unstiffens all our theories, limbers them up and sets each one at work."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Being nothing essentially new, it harmonizes with many ancient philosophic tendencies."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "It agrees with nominalism for instance, in always appealing to particulars; with utilitarianism in emphasizing practical aspects; with positivism in its disdain for verbal solutions, useless questions, and metaphysical abstractions."
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "All these, you see, are ANTI-INTELLECTUALIST tendencies."
[^7]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Against rationalism as a pretension and a method, pragmatism is fully armed and militant."
[^8]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "But, at the outset, at least, it stands for no particular results."
[^9]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "It has no dogmas, and no doctrines save its method."

# Pragmatism Lies Like a Corridor in a Hotel

As the young Italian pragmatist Papini has well said, pragmatism[^1] lies in the midst of our theories, like a corridor in a hotel.[^2] Innumerable chambers open out of it.[^3] In one you may find a man writing an atheistic volume; in the next someone on his knees praying for faith and strength; in a third a chemist investigating a body's properties.[^4] In a fourth a system of idealistic metaphysics is being excogitated; in a fifth the impossibility of metaphysics is being shown.[^5] But they all own the corridor, and all must pass through it if they want a practicable way of getting into or out of their respective rooms.[^6]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "pragmatism"
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "As the young Italian pragmatist Papini has well said, it lies in the midst of our theories, like a corridor in a hotel."
[^3]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Innumerable chambers open out of it."
[^4]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "In one you may find a man writing an atheistic volume; in the next someone on his knees praying for faith and strength; in a third a chemist investigating a body's properties."
[^5]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "In a fourth a system of idealistic metaphysics is being excogitated; in a fifth the impossibility of metaphysics is being shown."
[^6]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "But they all own the corridor, and all must pass through it if they want a practicable way of getting into or out of their respective rooms."

# The Pragmatic Method Is an Attitude of Orientation

No particular results then, so far, but only an attitude of orientation, is what the pragmatic method means.[^1] THE ATTITUDE OF LOOKING AWAY FROM FIRST THINGS, PRINCIPLES, 'CATEGORIES,' SUPPOSED NECESSITIES; AND OF LOOKING TOWARDS LAST THINGS, FRUITS, CONSEQUENCES, FACTS.[^2]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "No particular results then, so far, but only an attitude of orientation, is what the pragmatic method means."
[^2]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "THE ATTITUDE OF LOOKING AWAY FROM FIRST THINGS, PRINCIPLES, 'CATEGORIES,' SUPPOSED NECESSITIES; AND OF LOOKING TOWARDS LAST THINGS, FRUITS, CONSEQUENCES, FACTS."

# Pragmatism Also Means a Theory of Truth

Meanwhile the word pragmatism has come to be used in a still wider sense, as meaning also a certain theory of TRUTH.[^1]

[^1]: [[Pragmatism - Lecture II - What Pragmatism Means#The Method's Character and Affinities]] "Meanwhile the word pragmatism has come to be used in a still wider sense, as meaning also a certain theory of TRUTH."
